label: late original-phase positions (t>=7), plus digit 0 input from t>=5
explanation: Fires only while the original sequence is being read, at late absolute positions: 80% of steps at t=7 and 96% at t=8 (so only in sequences with L>=8), which is why it is concentrated on the final 1-2 original tokens. Inputting digit 0 at t>=5 triggers it almost every time (precision ~1.0), and those 0 inputs carry the largest activations: the top examples are all a 0 as the last original token at t=8, and t>=5 0-inputs hold ~27% of the activation mass. Other digits do not do this (widening the clause to all digits drops precision to 0.72). Weak residual firing at t=5-6 on other tokens and at the delimiter step for L=9 (~1% of mass). Never fires at t<=3 or during the copy phase. Dev F1 0.87, mass recall 0.96.

issues: The explanation's claims hold up. Test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.865, R 0.876, F1 0.870, mass recall 0.960). There is zero activation at t<=3 and in the copy phase. Original-phase firing rate is 0.80 at orig_idx 7 and 0.96 at orig_idx 8. The clause phase0 & t>=5 & in_tok==0 has precision 0.9997 and mass recall 0.27.

Minor inaccuracy: delimiter-step firing is not limited to L=9. On the dev split, the to_go breakdown shows 6424 delimiter-step activations for L=9 and 2522 for L=8. On test, delimiter firing has precision 0.077 for L=9 and 0.030 for L=8, and about 1% of mass in total.

Under-described token modulation: 0 is not the only token that affects activation. At t>=7, precision varies by input token: m 0.998, b 0.994, z 0.989, 1 0.988 versus t 0.45, n 0.58, g 0.71, k 0.74, s 0.75. At t=6 the same ordering appears (m 0.59, b 0.36, z 0.39, 1 0.27, a 0.22, versus t 0.001, n 0.005). So the 0 effect is the strongest end of a graded per-token preference. The claim that other digits 'do not behave this way' is only partly true, since 1 is also boosted. Most false positives at t>=7 come from low-preference tokens such as t and n.

There is no history dependence that would explain the false positives. Whether a 0 was seen earlier, the digit count and in_first all leave precision at t>=7 near 0.85. Neither adding t=6 & {m,b,z} nor removing t/n from the t>=7 clause improves F1 meaningfully (test F1 0.872 and 0.866), so this is a refinement rather than a systematic counterexample class.
The missed activations hold about 4% of mass and are mostly weak, scattered firing at t=5-6 and at the delimiter step.
